clue.text: Unselfish in good position in box

indicators.note: the second 'in' says the position term is placed inside the box word

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box
onside describes a player in a legal position in football or rugby

explanation.surface: Someone praised as generous while sitting comfortably in a theatre box.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to the phrase 'in good position'; the second 'in' is the container signal. ONSIDE is the football term for a player legally placed.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerate person thinks of others first, which is the core of being unselfish.

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a helping or portion of food is a ration

explanation.surface: Someone recovering on oxygen gets a portion of a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address, a kind of speech.

indicators.note: a breakdown here is the letters of the phrase collapsing into a new order

parts.note: read as 'nature is', so the S counts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood is said to be built into the natural world's collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdown' rearranges NATURESIN; here the 's of nature's stands for 'is' and gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sullen temperament, a synonym of melancholy.

indicators.note: about means the deceiving word goes around the picked letter

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating or deceiving them, so 'does'

indicators.note: a leader is the first, so the opening letter of labour is taken

explanation.surface: A Labour Party chief is accused of cheating over political gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L, the first letter of 'labour' (picked by 'leader's'), inside DOES. The capital-free 'labour' tempts a political reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Doles are portions handed out as charity, so they are donations.

clue.text: More crusty sailor up on deck

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor
a deck or level of a ship or stand is a tier

explanation.surface: An irritable old seaman climbs up on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the sailor word round; in a down entry it then sits on top of the deck word. 'Crusty' means irritable here, not having a crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattier is the comparative of ratty, meaning irritable, so more crusty or tetchy.

clue.text: It's time totter goes after rubbish

indicators.note: goes after means the movement word is written following the time abbreviation

parts.note: to totter is to walk unsteadily, to waddle

explanation.surface: A toddler wobbles off in pursuit of some litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is nonsense talk, which is rubbish in the figurative sense.

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of the two words are put together again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the letters I, T and S

explanation.surface: A war monument is reconstructed to honour the fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges MEMORIALITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To immortalise someone is to preserve their memory for ever, so to commemorate them.

clue.text: He won't stand for old people!

definitions.text: He won't stand for old people!

parts.words: He won't stand for old people!
parts.note: reads like a rude passenger refusing to give up a seat, but 'won't stand for' means will not tolerate

explanation.surface: A man stays seated on the bus rather than offering his place to the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prejudiced against the elderly refuses to tolerate them, discrimination by years.

clue.text: Asylum seeker's shouting, being put on plane

indicators.note: across, putting one word on another means attaching it after

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a rant is a loud, angry speech

explanation.surface: A refugee is shouting while being made to board an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'seeker's' stands for 'is' and links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A person seeking asylum has moved from their homeland, so is a migrant.

parts.note: to permit is to let
Hal is a familiar form of Harry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Someone named Harry holding a licence turns out to be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks round 'Harry' hint that it is a name to be swapped for another form of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means able to kill, a synonym of deadly.

indicators.note: redistributing means the letters are shared out again in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether sharing out income counts as the boldest business move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redistributing' rearranges REVENUEMOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Venturesome means willing to take risks, which is being bold or enterprising; 'most' here belongs to the fodder, so the definition is the plain adjective.

clue.text: Musical includes current and former actor

indicators.note: includes says the show's name holds the current symbol inside it

parts.note: Oliver! is a famous stage musical based on Oliver Twist
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A stage show's cast features a modern and a retired performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated twentieth-century English stage and film performer, now dead.

indicators.note: pinching means the rogue word grabs and holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible person, a rogue

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of damsel is removed, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A villain grabs a young woman in a cruel deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle of 'damsel'; 'pinching' puts what is left inside the rogue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a fraudulent scheme to cheat someone, a trick.

clue.text: Bird with a new strong man

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A muscleman is spotted with a little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant gods of Greek myth, so the word means a person of great strength or power.

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are knocked over and turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters N, U, T and S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crank's rule has come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges NUTSREIGN. 'Revolutionary' looks like it could signal the anagram, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel rising against government, so a revolutionary.

definitions.meaning: an office is a post or job
affairs as in the state of affairs, the circumstances

explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a paid position, which is an office, and also the overall circumstances, a state of affairs.

clue.text: Tell one is strangely more miserable

definitions.note: comparative in the clue, though the entry is the superlative form

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of the three words appear in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person describing how sad someone feels in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges TELLONEIS. The clue says 'more' where the superlative 'most' would match the entry exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Loneliest is the superlative of lonely, feeling isolated and sad, so the most miserable.

indicators.note: this 'in' places the saint inside the phrase meaning no drink

parts.note: zero means none, no
rum is an alcoholic spirit
a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A teetotal remedy offered by a virtuous fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, the abbreviation for saint, goes inside NO RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet remedy, so a cure.

parts.note: sounds like a prison break, since 'can' is slang for jail, but means liquid seeping from a tin

explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is fluid escaping through a hole, as from a punctured container.

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: A Greek poet's epic is a cracking read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'His odyssey makes excellent reading'; the whole clue also describes the Greek poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek poet credited with the Odyssey, a classic of great literature.

clue.text: Derby perhaps, houses a little home

indicators.note: houses means the hat word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat, an example of a hat
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: A racecourse is said to provide a small dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A derby is the American name for a bowler hat, though the surface suggests the English racecourse town.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where a creature lives, its home.

parts.note: a coaster is a small mat for a glass
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: An elderly ship sailing along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaster' suggests a coastal ship, but it is a drinks mat; in a down entry 'on' puts it above the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Mature means fully grown or advanced in years, so old.

indicators.note: following places the disgrace word after the reversed letters
backward means the abbreviation is written in reverse

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American
a stain on one's character is a shame or disgrace

explanation.surface: A diffident American must bear disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns the abbreviation round; the disgrace word follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a loss is to suffer or endure it.

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken and heard as a different spelling

parts.note: to massage dough or muscles is to knead it

explanation.surface: Someone desperate for a rub-down.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEADS, with its silent K, sounds like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that cries out for attention requires it, so it needs it.

indicators.note: engulfed by means the letters sit swallowed up inside the following words

explanation.surface: A shrub caught up in a pointless conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'war, but useless'. The arbutus is the strawberry tree, an evergreen shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus, or strawberry tree, is an evergreen shrub or small tree, a kind of bush.

indicators.note: taking means the stopping word takes in the letter for Republican

parts.note: to stop is to cease

explanation.surface: A call to stop following the Republican party line.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a fold mark, a line pressed into fabric or paper; in cricket it is also a marked line.

indicators.note: embracing means the fitness phrase wraps round the letter

parts.note: in trim means in good condition, fit
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A healthy performer hugs a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the middle of 'sweet', goes inside IN TRIM. 'Acting' looks theatrical but means temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim or acting manager holds a post temporarily until someone permanent arrives.

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the two words are in an unusual order

parts.note: read as 'primate is', so the S counts
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a monkey is an odd-looking creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges PRIMATESONE. 'Ape' is the verb, to mimic, not the animal the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them, to imitate them in manner.
